items: Portal Access: Search for your district's parent portal by typing "[Your District Name] parent portal" or "[Your District Name] PowerSchool parent login" to identify which platform your school uses.
Portal Login: Check your email and spam folder for parent portal activation information from your district, and call the school main office if you cannot locate it.
Notifications: Enable automatic notifications in the portal settings for new grades, missing assignments, and attendance issues so information reaches you without manual checking.
Portal Review: Check your child's missing assignments list in the parent portal every week since this view reveals where your child is falling behind before grades suffer.
Grade Check: Review your child's current grades by subject in the portal to understand which classes need attention and which are on track.
Scope Understanding: Recognize that the parent portal shows the official gradebook but not daily classroom activities, which live in Google Classroom, so you need both sources for a complete picture.
Weekly Habit: Set a recurring weekly calendar reminder to log into the parent portal and review your child's academic status so checking becomes a consistent habit.
Classroom Distinction: Understand that the portal is the official record that determines grades and promotion, but it represents the floor, not the ceiling, of what your child is actually learning.
Daily Questions: Ask your child specific questions about what they are working on in Google Classroom and their Chromebook rather than the vague "what did you learn today?" question that gets shrugs.

Communication Strategy: Email or message teachers directly through the portal or Google Classroom rather than waiting for school-wide communications that may not address your child's specific situation.
Advocacy Action: Stop feeling guilty about being frustrated with the digital learning system and instead update your approach by learning the tools your child's school uses.
Progress Tracking: Compare your child's grades and missing assignments week over week in the portal to identify patterns and intervene early when you see a decline.
